title: Protocol for detecting Yersinia pseudotuberculosis nitric oxide exposure during in vitro growth
protocol: Dilute bacterial cells 1:50 into fresh LB or fresh LB + DETA NONOate from overnight cultures.
Add 60 μL of overnight culture to 3 mL LB or LB + DETA NONOate for each tube.
Collect cells for the t = 0 timepoint.
Aliquot 500 μL from each culture tube.
Put 200 μL into a 96-well plate and 300 μL into a microcentrifuge tube.
Place the microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Incubate culture tubes at 37°C with rotation at 50 rpm in a rotor or in an orbital shaker at 200 rpm.
Add LB only into one well of a 96-well plate to serve as a blank.
Check the OD600 of t = 0 samples using a plate reader, with a blank well containing LB without bacteria.
Subtract the OD600 value from the blank well from sample values to obtain true absorbance.
Transfer the entire 200 μL out of each well into corresponding microcentrifuge tubes, keeping an additional 300 μL on ice for microscopy analysis.
Centrifuge samples in microcentrifuge tubes at 15,000 rpm (20,627 × g) for 1 minute at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant by aspirating.
Resuspend each pellet with 200 μL of 4% PFA.
Allow fixation of samples for 12-16 hours at 4°C in the dark or covered with aluminum foil.
Incubate the culture tubes with rotation (50 rpm in a rotor, or in an orbital shaker at 200 rpm) at 37°C for a total of 4 h.
Every 2 h, repeat steps as necessary until 4 h.
Check the plate reader raw data to ensure cells incubated in LB + DETA NONOate are growth-arrested compared to samples grown in LB only (lower A600 nm, no change in values between t = 0 and t = 4 h).
Dissolve 1% agarose in PBS using a microwave.
Place the beaker containing the agarose solution on a heat block set at 70°C to prevent solidification.
Use the smallest volume beaker possible.
Add strips of labeling tape to microscope slides, ensuring they are firmly adhered.
Place prepared slides on a 70°C heat block.
Cut the end off a 20–200 μL pipet tip to create a beveled edge.
Set the pipet to 50 μL for dispensing approximately 20 μL of agarose solution.
Pipette 20 μL of agarose onto the slide between the strips of tape.
Immediately place a cover slip on top of the agarose on the slide.
Allow the agarose pad to cool at room temperature for 20 minutes.
After the agarose solidifies, remove the first coverslip with a razor blade.
Set the pipette volume to 50 μL (this will dispense approximately 25 μL).
Pipette 1% agarose from the beaker and immediately add it between the tape strips on the slide.
Immediately place a fresh coverslip over the agarose.
Allow the agarose to spread on the slide surface for about 3–5 seconds before removing the slide from the heat block.
Let the agarose solidify at room temperature for approximately 20 minutes.
Use a razor blade to carefully peel off the coverslip.
Carefully remove the tape strips.
Clean any excess agarose off of the slide.
Cut off the edges of the agarose pad if necessary, ensuring it is flat and even.
Take out the fixed bacterial cells from the 4°C refrigerator.
Centrifuge samples in a tabletop microcentrifuge at 15,000 rpm (20,627 × g) for 1 minute at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant by aspirating.
Resuspend cells in 50 μL of 1× PBS.
Add 5–8 μL fixed bacteria to the center of the agarose.
Place a fresh coverslip on top.
Proceed immediately to Major Step Three.
Optional: Store fixed cells resuspended in PBS at 4°C for a few days.
Prepare samples from the NO exposure experiment for imaging via fluorescence microscopy.
Position the sample under a 63× oil immersion objective with a numerical aperture of 1.4.
Take 5 images at distinctly different fields of view using fluorescence microscopy.
Choose fields of view that contain single cells or cells more spread apart for single cell analysis.
Use image analysis software to identify bacterial cells by their constitutive GFP signal and size.
Apply a size selection criterion of 1 μm² to 6 μm² to select for single cells.
Exclude aggregates and doublets indicated by multiple bacteria from the analysis.
Use a Zeiss Axio Observer.Z1 fluorescent microscope for imaging bacterial cells.
Utilize DIC, GFP, and mCherry channels when imaging the strain used in the experiment.
Focus on bacterial cells using the DIC channel.
Avoid focusing or scanning using fluorescent channels to prevent photobleaching.
Maintain consistent exposure times for GFP and mCherry channels between samples and replicates.
Determine optimal exposure times by examining both mCherry+ and mCherry- samples beforehand.
Perform single cell analysis using Volocity software.
Convert CVI images from Zeiss software into ZVI images.
Use constitutive GFP signal as reference to identify bacteria as objects.
Specify size range of objects from 1 μm² to 6 μm².
Exclude objects larger or smaller than the specified size range.
Crop images if agarose pad is uneven and causes bacteria to be in different planes of view.
Record mean single cell GFP signals for each image.
Record mean single cell mCherry signals for each image.
Compile measurements using Volocity software's Measurement item function.
Export compiled data into a single excel spreadsheet.
Graph and perform further statistical analyses as needed.
Open images in ImageJ/Fiji in their raw format.
Select 'split channels' in the Bio-Formats Import Options tab.
Keep all other default options for image import.
In MicrobeJ, under the ‘Images’ tab, change ‘Image’ to ‘Channel(s)’.
Assign ‘C=1’ to ‘Ch. 1’ for mCherry and ‘C=0’ to ‘Ch. 2’ for GFP.
Click the camera icon to merge images into a hyperstack.
Select the channel associated with GFP (Channel 2).
Change ‘Medial Axis’ to ‘Fit Shape’ in the first dropdown menu below.
Set area (μm²) to 1–6 and click the blue play button at the bottom of this dialog box.
Measure the mean mCherry intensity for each cell using the formula “mCh int mean = bacteria.INTENSITY.ch1.mean”.
Generate a new column in the table named “mCh int mean” with the mean fluorescence intensity of mCherry for each bacterial cell.
Measure the mean GFP intensity for each cell using the formula “GFP int mean = bacteria.INTENSITY.ch2.mean”.
Generate a new column in the table named “GFP int mean” with the mean fluorescence intensity of GFP for each bacterial cell.
